San Francisco Administrative Code § 37.3 — Rent Limitations
sources.agency: City and County of San Francisco / Rent Board
sources.quote: A landlord who has reported the required information about their rental unit to the Rent Board as set forth in Section 37.15 shall have a license to impose annually a rent increase which does not exceed a tenant's base rent by more than 60% of said published increase. In no event, however, shall the allowable annual increase be greater than 7%. … (b) Notice of Rent Increase for Tenants in Occupancy … (1) Which portion of the rent increase reflects the annual increase, and/or a banked amount, if any … (5) Nonconforming Rent Increases. Any rent increase which does not conform with the provisions of this section shall be null and void. … (a)(11)(A) a landlord may not impose increases solely because a tenant has added an additional occupant to an existing tenancy … (d)(2)(B) This Subsection shall not apply to partial changes in occupancy of a dwelling or unit where one or more of the occupants … remains an occupant in lawful possession.
sources.date_of_document: Current code text as published on sf.gov

sources.title: Rent Board Rules and Regulations, Part I — §§ 1.11 and 1.12
sources.quote: The anniversary date is the date on which the tenant's current rent became effective … The next allowable rent increase shall take effect no less than one year from the anniversary date … In no event, however, shall the allowable annual increase be greater than seven percent (7%).

sources.title: Rent Board Rules and Regulations, Part IV — §§ 4.10 and 4.12
sources.quote: Section 4.10 Notice (a) … shall inform the tenant in writing on or before the date the notice is given of the following: (1) Which portion of the rent increase reflects the annual increase, and/or banked amount, if any … Section 4.12 Banking (a) … the rent may be increased only one time every twelve (12) months … A full 12 months must have elapsed from the date that an annual rent increase, or a portion thereof, could have been imposed before this banking section becomes applicable. Banked increases shall not be compounded and shall not be rounded up.

sources.title: Learn about rent increases in San Francisco
sources.quote: A landlord can impose the first annual increase 12 months after the date the tenant's lease began. … A landlord must get a rent increase license before imposing annual allowable and/or banked rent increases on a tenant. … 30-day written notice of the proposed rent increase; 90-day written notice if the increase … is more than 10%. If the notice is mailed, the landlord must give the tenant 5 more days. … A landlord cannot charge additional rent simply because a new (or additional) roommate has moved into a unit with the existing tenant. … There is no limit on how much rent a landlord may first charge a tenant when renting an empty unit that is covered by rent control.

sources.title: Banked rent increases
sources.quote: A skipped increase is only banked if at least 24 full months pass without any rent increase. If less than 24 months pass, the skipped increase is lost and cannot be imposed at a later date. … Once an increase is properly banked, it does not expire. … Banked increases do not carry over to a new tenant. … They cannot be compounded or prorated. … 30-day written notice of the proposed rent increase; 90-day written notice if the increase … is more than 10%.

sources.title: Annual rent increase for multiple years
sources.quote: In these situations, landlords may increase rent by adding up the allowable increases during that time period. … Increases cannot be compounded. Landlords are not required to file a petition with the City to impose these types of rent increases. Landlords cannot 'round up' to the nearest dollar … Landlords must give at least 30-days notice in writing before any increase goes into effect (or 35-days if sent by mail).

sources.title: Learn about San Francisco rental laws
sources.quote: Many residential units built on or before June 13, 1979 have both rent control and eviction protection. … If your unit was built before June 14, 1979, and is not used as a single family dwelling, it may have both: Rent control; Eviction protection. … The first step is to find out when your building was built. You can search your address on the Property Information Map. … Some units are hard to classify. If you are unsure about your unit then you should speak with a Rent Board counselor. … Weekday free counseling hours (9 am to noon and 1 to 4pm).

sources.title: The Rent Board Housing Inventory
sources.quote: All owners of residential property are required to report. … A landlord must have a current rent increase license on file with the Rent Board before any annual or banked rent increase can go into effect. … March 1 of every year. … The information entered in the housing inventory submission is public. … You will still need to comply with all other local and state rent increase laws.

sources.title: Notice of Owner Noncompliance with Housing Inventory
sources.quote: If the unit is rent-controlled and you issued a rent increase that went into effect when no license was on record, your tenant may be entitled to a rent refund. … A rent increase notice that goes into effect while the unit is unlicensed may be null and void (this may apply for multiple years). … Owners of condominiums and buildings with less than 10 residential units have been required to report since March 1, 2023.

sources.title: Notification of 2027 Rent Board Fee and Housing Inventory Requirements
sources.quote: A new law requires all owners of residential property in San Francisco to annually report information about their units into the Rent Board's Housing Inventory database separate from the fee assessment [Ordinance No. 265-20]. … Landlords will not receive a license to impose annual and/or banked rent increases until reporting is complete. … Some rent increases given without a license will be null and void. … Deadline to report: March 1, 2027, and annually by March 1 of each year.

sources.title: Press release: Rent Board Reminds Property Owners of the March 1st Housing Inventory Reporting Deadline
sources.quote: Thus far, the San Francisco Rent Board has issued 12,000 licenses to permit owners to impose rent increases for the next year. That represents less than 5% of the estimated number of residential units in San Francisco. … Owners of properties with fewer than 10 units, including condos and single-family homes, are now also required to report into the Inventory annually.

sources.title: Landlord Petitions and Passthroughs
sources.quote: For certain types of rent increases, landlords must file a petition at the Rent Board before serving the tenants with a notice of the increase. … There are six types of rent increases that require the filing of a landlord petition: Capital Improvement Passthrough; Operating and Maintenance Expense Increase; Special Circumstances Increase Based on Rents for Comparable Units; Rent Increase Based on the Past Rent History of a Proposition I Affected Unit; Utility Passthrough; Rules and Regulations Section 1.21 Increase … There is no charge for filing a Rent Board petition.

sources.title: Roommates and subletting
sources.quote: Landlords in San Francisco cannot charge more rent simply because a new roommate (or several) has moved into a unit. This is illegal, no matter what the lease itself says. Any agreement to pay more rent is void and unenforceable by the landlord. … Landlords can increase the rent to market rate in some situations when the original tenants have moved out.

sources.title: Rent Increases Under Section 6.14 And Costa-Hawkins
sources.quote: Costa-Hawkins provides that when the last original occupant no longer permanently resides in the unit, the landlord may impose an unlimited rent increase on a lawful subtenant or assignee who did not reside in the unit prior to January 1, 1996. … In addition, a co-tenant, as opposed to a subtenant, is not subject to such a rent increase, regardless of when the co-tenant moved in. … Since these provisions can be complicated, landlords and tenants should obtain legal advice concerning their application to specific fact situations.

sources.title: Petition for a Determination Pursuant to Section 6.14 and/or Costa-Hawkins
sources.quote: San Francisco's Rent Ordinance does not regulate the initial rent for a new tenancy, so landlords are permitted to set rents for new tenancies at market rate. … any co-tenant who moved in after the original occupant is not subject to such a rent increase, regardless of when the co-tenant moved in. A co-tenant is someone who has an oral or written agreement with the landlord, or who the landlord has treated as a tenant by the acceptance of rent or other conduct. … landlords and tenants are strongly encouraged to seek legal advice.

sources.title: Report an unlawful rent increase or request a review of your rent history
sources.quote: There is no charge for filing the petition. There is no time limit for filing a petition. … Usually within a few months after the petition is filed, it will be scheduled for an arbitration hearing before a Rent Board Administrative Law Judge. … The hearing process is designed so that no one needs an attorney, although parties are entitled to have an attorney or other authorized representative assist them at the hearing.

sources.title: Rent Board Forms Center
sources.quote: 516C: Unlawful Rent Increase — This petition is for tenants who have received an unlawful rent increase and/ or want the Rent Board to determine whether their current rent is a lawful amount. … 518: Tenant Summary Petition (for pending unlawful rent increase) — This petition is for tenants who have received a rent increase notice that is clearly unlawful on its face and has not yet gone into effect.

sources.title: Speak with a Rent Board counselor
sources.quote: Cost: Free … We provide counseling on subjects related to the Rent Ordinance. We cannot give legal advice. We will let you know when your question is one that should be answered by a lawyer.

sources.title: Rent Board Referral Listing (January 2025)
sources.quote: The Rent Board cannot refer you to individual attorneys, but staff will be glad to direct you to appropriate resources for advice and assistance. Please note that you do not need a lawyer to file a petition at the Rent Board. … Three free legal clinics every month for low-income Bay Area residents. The clinics offer free, limited legal advice and referrals. … Landlord Resources: Small Property Owners of San Francisco.

sources.title: General Eviction Notice requirements
sources.quote: If you are a tenant who has received eviction court papers, you can call 415-659-9184, email legal@evictiondefense.org, or visit the Eviction Defense Collaborative for free legal help.

sources.title: Housing Trust Fund Five-Year Report 2019–2023 (Tenant Right to Counsel)
sources.agency: San Francisco Mayor's Office of Housing and Community Development
sources.quote: In June 2018, San Francisco voters passed the No Eviction Without Representation Act to establish the Tenant Right to Counsel program, which provides free legal assistance for residents facing eviction and free full-scope legal assistance for eligible cases. … An ongoing challenge for the right to counsel program has been the difficulty in identifying sufficient attorneys with the skills necessary to provide full scope legal representation.

sources.title: California Civil Code § 827 — notice of rent increase
sources.quote: If the proposed rent increase for that tenant is 10 percent or less … the notice shall be delivered at least 30 days before the effective date of the increase … If the proposed rent increase for that tenant is greater than 10 percent … the notice shall be delivered at least 90 days before the effective date of the increase … By delivering a copy to the tenant personally. By serving a copy by mail under the procedures prescribed in Section 1013 of the Code of Civil Procedure.

sources.title: California Civil Code § 1947.12 — Tenant Protection Act rent cap
sources.quote: An owner of residential real property shall not, over the course of any 12-month period, increase the gross rental rate for a dwelling or a unit more than 5 percent plus the percentage change in the cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower … the gross rental rate … shall not be increased in more than two increments over that 12-month period … (d)(3) Housing subject to rent or price control through a public entity's valid exercise of its police power … that restricts annual increases in the rental rate to an amount less than that provided in subdivision (a).

sources.title: California Civil Code § 1954.53 — Costa-Hawkins Rental Housing Act
sources.quote: (d)(2) If the original occupant or occupants who took possession of the dwelling or unit pursuant to the rental agreement with the owner no longer permanently reside there, an owner may increase the rent by any amount allowed by this section to a lawful sublessee or assignee who did not reside at the dwelling or unit prior to January 1, 1996. (d)(3) This subdivision does not apply to partial changes in occupancy of a dwelling or unit where one or more of the occupants of the premises … remains an occupant in lawful possession of the dwelling or unit.
sources.date_of_document: Amended by Stats. 2023, Ch. 767, Sec. 1 (AB 1620), effective 2024-01-01

sources.title: California Government Code § 12955 — housing discrimination (FEHA)
sources.quote: It shall be unlawful: (a) For the owner of any housing accommodation to discriminate against or harass any person because of the race, color, religion, sex, gender, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, marital status, national origin, ancestry, familial status, source of income, disability, veteran or military status, or genetic information of that person. … (f) For any owner of housing accommodations to harass, evict, or otherwise discriminate against any person … when the owner's dominant purpose is retaliation against a person who has opposed practices unlawful under this section.

sources.title: The California Tenant Protection Act of 2019 (AB 1482) — SF Rent Board summary
sources.quote: The maximum rent increase for units under AB 1482 from August 1, 2026 to July 31, 2027 is 8.8% in San Francisco. This does NOT apply for units under the rent increase limitations of the San Francisco Rent Ordinance. … If a unit is already covered by San Francisco's local eviction and/or rent increase regulations, the unit remains subject to those local regulations … But the Rent Board does not provide legal advice and cannot enforce state law or conduct hearings on disputes about AB 1482. AB 1482 can only be enforced in state court.

sources.title: 42 U.S.C. § 3604 — Discrimination in the sale or rental of housing (U.S. Code)
sources.agency: U.S. Government Publishing Office / Office of the Law Revision Counsel
sources.quote: (b) To discriminate against any person in the terms, conditions, or privileges of sale or rental of a dwelling, or in the provision of services or facilities in connection therewith, because of race, color, religion, sex, familial status, or national origin. … (f)(2) To discriminate against any person in the terms, conditions, or privileges of sale or rental of a dwelling … because of a handicap.

sources.quote: The Fair Housing Act prohibits discrimination in housing because of: Race; Color; National Origin; Religion; Sex; Familial Status; Disability.

sources.title: 24 CFR § 100.65 — Discrimination in terms, conditions and privileges

sources.title: Partial Exemption for Certain Single-Family Homes and Condominiums Under Costa-Hawkins
sources.quote: A single-family dwelling with a legal in-law unit constitutes a two-unit building and is not exempt from the Ordinance. A single-family dwelling with an illegal in-law unit also constitutes a two-unit building and is not exempt, unless both units are rented together as a single tenancy. A single-family dwelling is not exempt if there is another residential structure on the same lot.
